subject: Arabic

source.title: Junior School Curriculum Design — Arabic Grade 7 (First published 2022, Revised 2024)
source.notes: Read in full via the Read tool (native PDF text extraction, no pages param, per CURRICULUM-MINING-GUIDE.md) directly from designs/. Structure: 3 strands (1.0 Listening and Speaking, 2.0 Reading, 3.0 Writing), each built around the same 9 real-world themes used by Arabic/French/German/Mandarin at Grades 8-9 (Greetings and Introduction, Family, My Surrounding, Time, Fun and Enjoyment, Food and Drinks, My Body, Weather and Environment, Getting Around) = 27 sub-strands (1.1-1.9, 2.1-2.9, 3.1-3.9), each 2 sessions, plus a standalone 6-lesson 'Showcasing of skills and concepts (Exhibition)' allocation = 60 lessons total, matching the summary table on p.x. KNOWN SOURCE-DOCUMENT TYPO: sub-strand 2.7's page header literally reads 'THEME 7: FOOD AND DRINKS' a second time, but its actual Specific Learning Outcomes / Suggested Learning Experiences are unambiguously about physical-appearance description (identify descriptive words, describe physical appearance via picture reading, reader's theatre) — i.e. it is really the strand's 'My Body' theme, matching Listening&Speaking 1.7 and Writing 3.7 which are both correctly labelled 'My Body'. Recorded below under theme 'My Body' with the typo noted, not treated as a real second Food-and-Drinks sub-strand. Only Theme 1 (Greetings) supplies actual romanized Arabic example phrases in the source document itself ('ayna taskun?' = where do you live?, 'maa ismu sadeeqak?' = what is your friend's name?); the other 8 themes describe target vocabulary only in English, so vocabulary for those themes reuses the same vetted romanized-Arabic word bank already used and spot-checked in this project's Grade 8/9 Arabic skill files (same 9 shared themes), per the 'don't fabricate vocabulary beyond a vetted bank' discipline used for Grade 9 Arabic's own sourcing.

essenceNote: Kenya is part of the international community and therefore the learners shall be given an opportunity to learn foreign languages in addition to the national, official and indigenous languages. These foreign languages include: Arabic, French, German and Mandarin. The Learner is expected to acquire the four language skills: listening, speaking, reading and writing at a basic level in the curriculum. Foreign languages learning at this level is guided by social-constructivism and environmental theories. The learner will transit to Senior School having acquired basic proficiency equivalent to A1/YCT2 (verbatim essence statement, p.viii).

generalLearningOutcomes.scope: By the end of Junior School (Grades 7-9 combined)
outcomes: Listen and respond appropriately to relevant information in the Arabic language.
Read a wide variety of texts fluently and accurately for lifelong learning.
Write texts legibly, coherently and creatively in the Arabic language.
Express themselves fluently and confidently in varied contexts.
Appreciate the role of Arabic language as a means of embracing creativity and international relevance.
Enjoy communicating in the Arabic language.
Appreciate cultural awareness and exposure to the Arabic language.

subStrands.name: Listening for Gist
specificLearningOutcomes: identify the main idea in a spoken text
respond to simple questions on greetings and introduction of self and others
develop interest in learning Arabic
learningExperiences: listen to an audio recording on greetings and introduction
collaborate with peers to analyse concepts to identify the main idea in the recorded text
work with peers to answer questions while accommodating diverse opinions, e.g. 'where do you live? (ayna taskun?)', 'What is your friend's name? (maa ismu sadeeqak?)'
role play greetings and introduction of friends of different gender
keyInquiryQuestions: How can you extract the main idea in a given text?
scopeNotes: include: role play must cover greetings/introductions of friends of different gender (gender-issues PCI)

subStrands.name: Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation
specificLearningOutcomes: identify family members by their names and professions
apply appropriate intonation and stress in pronouncing words for fluency
appreciate the role of immediate family members for social co-existence
learningExperiences: identify family members by their names and professions
talk about their immediate family members with peers actively, e.g. 'where does your parents work?'
use appropriate intonation and stress when asking questions related to the theme
team up to record each other applying intonation/stress in speech, peer assess for constructive feedback
collaborate with peers to compose a song on various professions
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is it good to pronounce words correctly?
scopeNotes: include: professions vocabulary, not just family-relation terms — SLO (a) explicitly names 'names and professions'

subStrands.name: Phonological Awareness
specificLearningOutcomes: pronounce words related to the theme appropriately
apply appropriate stress and intonation for fluency
develop interest pronouncing Arabic words correctly
learningExperiences: listen to audio-visual recordings about the market using digital devices
identify vocabulary related to the theme used in the recording
work jointly to practise pronouncing the words accurately
role play a market scene involving buying and selling of items, using appropriate stress/intonation
keyInquiryQuestions: What can you do to improve your ability to pronounce words accurately?

subStrands.name: Listening for Gist
specificLearningOutcomes: identify key ideas from a spoken text related to the theme
use acquired vocabulary to make sentences for comprehension
acknowledge important dates and holidays for lifelong learning
learningExperiences: listen attentively to a presentation on important dates in the calendar
pick out key ideas from the recorded presentation on various dates in the calendar
work with peers to practise pronouncing the dates while showing respect for each other
make an oral presentation using simple sentences on important dates, that is, Eid, Holidays
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we pick out key ideas from a text?
scopeNotes: include: Eid and Holidays are the source's own named examples of important dates

subStrands.name: Listening for Information
subStrands.notes: 2 sessions — identifying specific details, verbal instructions
specificLearningOutcomes: identify specific information from an oral text for information
respond to simple verbal instructions correctly
acknowledge the role of listening keenly for lifelong learning
learningExperiences: listen to an audio recording on activities carried out for fun and enjoyment
collaborate with peers to answer direct and inferential questions on the recording
play a language game involving use of verbal instructions e.g. the 'Simon says' language game
engage in a dialogue with peers on how leisure time should be used
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we extract specific information from a text?
scopeNotes: include: a verbal-instruction / 'Simon says' style activity, not just leisure-activity vocabulary

subStrands.name: Phonological Awareness
specificLearningOutcomes: pronounce vocabulary accurately for fluency
use acquired vocabulary to describe an event fluently
appreciate fluency in speech using acquired vocabulary
learningExperiences: engage in a collaborative conversation on the prices of different items from a given display of price lists
work jointly to practise pronouncing words related to the theme correctly
use acquired vocabulary to role play a dialogue between a shop assistant and customers
keyInquiryQuestions: How does vocabulary building help in learning Arabic language?

subStrands.name: Imitative Speaking
specificLearningOutcomes: identify words used to describe people and things
describe different things and events using relevant descriptive words
appreciate vocabulary building for language acquisition
learningExperiences: search for words used to describe people and things from print and online sources
practise pronouncing vocabulary on physical appearance descriptors
observe different pictures from a given display and describe the appearances of the people using relevant descriptors
take turns to talk about their friend or family members
keyInquiryQuestions: How does vocabulary help in learning a language?

subStrands.name: Conversational Skills
specificLearningOutcomes: identify nonverbal cues used for effective communication
use appropriate non-verbal cues in oral presentations
develop interest in speaking skills
learningExperiences: watch a video presentation related to the theme
work jointly to identify non-verbal cues used in presentations e.g. gestures, general appearance, tonal variation, movement, facial expressions
collaborate with peers to demonstrate the various non-verbal cues and what they imply
make a presentation to peers using appropriate non-verbal cues, peer assess for correct use of non-verbal cues
discuss common non-verbal cues that may contradict the message being spoken
keyInquiryQuestions: Why are non-verbal cues key in communication?
scopeNotes: include: the 5 named non-verbal cue types (gestures, general appearance, tonal variation, movement, facial expressions) as testable content, not just weather vocabulary — this sub-strand is genuinely about communication technique

subStrands.name: Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation
specificLearningOutcomes: identify vocabulary related to the theme from an oral text
use accurate pronunciation in target words for fluency
appreciate the role of fluency in effective communication
learningExperiences: watch a video clip and answer questions on different places in the locality in groups e.g. market, school, hospital, mosques
describe different places within the locality using related vocabulary
engage in a conversation locating different places in the locality using appropriate pronunciation of target words
take turns to practise pronouncing words using minimal pairs fluently
keyInquiryQuestions: How can you improve your speaking skill?
scopeNotes: include: market, school, hospital, mosques are the source's own named example locality places

subStrands.name: Reading Aloud: Fluency
specificLearningOutcomes: differentiate words and phrases based on their pronunciation correctly
read simple sentences on basic introductions fluently
develop interest in reading Arabic texts for enjoyment
learningExperiences: read words and phrases while underlining huruf shamsiyya and huruf qamariyyah from a given display
read short sentences on greetings and introductions fluently
use think-pair-share to read and complete simple sentences
practise reading from variety of texts at home
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is fluency important?
scopeNotes: include: huruf shamsiyya (sun letters) vs huruf qamariyyah (moon letters) — the definite-article 'al-' pronunciation rule — is the sub-strand's own named distinguishing content, not decoration

subStrands.name: Reading for Comprehension
subStrands.notes: 2 sessions — vocabulary building, inferring meaning of words
specificLearningOutcomes: identify target words and phrases in a written text
infer meaning of new words in a text
appreciate vocabulary building for language acquisition
learningExperiences: read simple sentences in a text and circle familiar words and phrases
pick out vocabulary from a text related to the theme, build a vocabulary bank
work jointly to infer meaning of words from context
use the vocabulary acquired to make sentences
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we derive meaning of a new word in texts?

subStrands.name: Reading Aloud: Fluency
specificLearningOutcomes: read short and simple sentences fluently
use appropriate pace to read simple texts for fluency
read texts in Arabic for enjoyment
learningExperiences: take turns to read aloud short sentences about the market
team up to conduct a reading speed contest for fluency
time each other's reading speed and identify the best reading speed
discuss disadvantages of other reading speeds and reasons for the selected speed
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is reading at the right speed important?

subStrands.name: Reading for Comprehension
specificLearningOutcomes: pronounce target words accurately for effective communication
respond to questions on a text for comprehension
develop interest in reading Arabic texts
learningExperiences: identify vocabulary words from a written text, pronounce them correctly
use minimal pairs to practise pronouncing target sounds and letters
collaborate with peers to respond to direct and inferential questions
keyInquiryQuestions: How can you improve your fluency in reading skills?

subStrands.name: Reading Aloud: Fluency
subStrands.notes: 2 sessions — vocabulary building, intonation, reading speed
specificLearningOutcomes: read target vocabulary in a given text
read a short passage with proper intonation and appropriate speed
develop interest in reading Arabic texts fluently
learningExperiences: read a range of texts aloud about leisure time and answer questions
isolate new words and search for their meaning
read a given passage focusing on correct pronunciation of consonants and verbs
team up to participate in a reading competition, peer assess for correct intonation and speed
keyInquiryQuestions: How does reading speed affect communication?

subStrands.name: Reading for Information
specificLearningOutcomes: identify locations where various foods are bought
summarise ideas presented in a written text for comprehension
read Arabic texts for enjoyment
learningExperiences: identify locations where foods and drinks are found
read a simple paragraph related to the theme, summarize key ideas
derive meaning of vocabulary identified from the paragraph, match vocabulary to its meaning
read level appropriate text independently during free time
keyInquiryQuestions: How can you paraphrase a long text without losing out on key ideas?

subStrands.name: Reading Aloud: Fluency
subStrands.notes: 2 sessions — adjectives (descriptive words), pronunciation. SOURCE TYPO: page header literally repeats 'THEME 7: FOOD AND DRINKS' but SLOs/content are unambiguously physical-appearance description — recorded here under its real theme, 'My Body', matching Listening&Speaking 1.7 and Writing 3.7.
specificLearningOutcomes: identify descriptive words from a text for comprehension
read a passage related to the theme using correct pronunciation for fluency
acknowledge the need for correct pronunciation for effective communication
learningExperiences: read short passages aloud on physical appearance and answer questions
pick out descriptive words from the text
describe the physical appearance of people through picture reading from a digital device
conduct a reader's theatre to read a passage using correct pronunciation
organise a language reading club for future use
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is reading fluently important?

subStrands.name: Reading for Comprehension
specificLearningOutcomes: identify the various clothing used for different weather seasons
respond to questions based on the theme for comprehension
advocate for reading of Arabic texts for enjoyment
learningExperiences: practise reading short passages on seasons with appropriate speed
identify clothing used at different weather seasons
organise the information on a chart for comprehension
collaborate to answer questions on the text read
memorise and recite poems about weather
keyInquiryQuestions: How does change of seasons affect our daily activities?
Why are comprehension questions important?
scopeNotes: include: clothing-per-season is the sub-strand's explicit named angle, not bare weather-word recall

subStrands.name: Extensive Reading: Library Skills
subStrands.notes: 2 sessions — selecting texts, tracking reading progress
specificLearningOutcomes: select a reading text from a collection of materials
track the reading progress for self-assessment
develop a positive attitude towards reading
learningExperiences: discuss issues to consider when selecting a reading text from a collection of materials
read a text aloud on locating places in the locality and talk about it
participate in reading circles by reading varied texts related to the theme
prepare a vocabulary bank on words identified from the texts
prepare a reading log to track the reading progress for self-assessment
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we easily and safely locate places in our environment?
Why should we keep a record of texts read?
scopeNotes: This sub-strand's real content is library/reading-habit skills (choosing a text, tracking a reading log), not vocabulary recall — build accordingly.

subStrands.name: Guided Writing: Handwriting
subStrands.notes: 2 sessions — neatness and legibility, simple sentences
specificLearningOutcomes: write target words neatly and legibly
use vocabulary to make sentences on introduction of friends for comprehension
develop interest in writing Arabic
learningExperiences: listen to a recording on greetings/introductions, write the specific greetings mentioned
list common names of friends on flashcards
identify vocabulary on greetings and introduction, construct simple sentences
share sentences with peers for review
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is greeting important?
How can we ensure we write texts neatly and legibly?
scopeNotes: This app has no handwriting-tracing UI — express 'neatness/legibility' as correct-spelling/well-formed-sentence content instead, per project precedent for handwriting sub-strands.

subStrands.name: Guided Writing: Spelling
subStrands.notes: 2 sessions — vocabulary building, spelling, neatness and legibility
specificLearningOutcomes: list different professions using correct spelling
use acquired vocabulary to make sentences neatly and legibly
appreciate neat and legible handwriting for effective communication
learningExperiences: list various professions on charts, share for peer review on spelling

keyInquiryQuestions: How can you ensure correct spelling of words when writing?
scopeNotes: include: professions vocabulary explicitly, matching SLO (a)

subStrands.name: Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing
specificLearningOutcomes: identify places where things are bought for comprehension

learningExperiences: identify various places where foods and drinks are bought
build a collection of vocabulary based on the theme

subStrands.name: Guided Writing: Sequencing Ideas
subStrands.notes: 2 sessions — vocabulary building, coherence, paragraph writing
specificLearningOutcomes: list the festivals and holidays celebrated at different times of the year for information

learningExperiences: listen to a recording on festivals/holidays celebrated at different times, make a list

keyInquiryQuestions: How can we present ideas in a paragraph in correct sequence?
scopeNotes: include: festivals/holidays (Eid) reordering-into-coherent-paragraph is this sub-strand's explicit content — a natural fit for an ordering QuestionKind branch

subStrands.name: Guided Writing: Imaginative Writing
subStrands.notes: 2 sessions — features of a composition, composing an imaginative composition
specificLearningOutcomes: identify features of an imaginative writing for information

learningExperiences: research features of imaginative writing from print and non-print sources

subStrands.name: Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation
specificLearningOutcomes: identify punctuation marks used in writing Arabic texts

learningExperiences: identify punctuation marks used in Arabic texts, draw on charts

How do punctuation marks contribute to meaning in texts?
scopeNotes: This app uses the romanized/Latin punctuation marks (full stop, comma, question mark, exclamation mark) since Arabic-script-specific punctuation isn't renderable without Arabic script in this app's typed-answer fields.

subStrands.name: Guided Writing: Poetry

subStrands.name: Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing
subStrands.notes: 2 sessions — key ideas, coherence in paragraphs, neatness and legibility
